rules_proposed.rule: A room whose label names a multi-use function (play, activity, relaxation) is typed 'living' and its furniture is judged against the living-room program; a bench is a valid piece of a living room, so the 'bench is not a piece of a living room' refusal is a false alarm and the room type 'other' is the misread.

A dining chair's clearance to the wall or piece behind it is measured from the chair's backrest, not its seat edge; when the drawn chair is 0.78 m from the table edge to the wall and the chair depth is 0.55 m, the backrest-to-wall clearance is 0.23 m, which is below the 0.45 m minimum, so the finding is real and the chair must be moved or the table shifted.

A tv_unit's back must be on a wall; when the drawn position is 1.01 m off the nearest wall and no free wall span exists (doors, windows block every span), the tv_unit is a misread of a wall-mounted tv or a console that belongs on a different wall, and the general rule is that a tv_unit drawn in the middle of a room with no wall behind it is a misread and must be retyped or moved to the nearest wall span.

A 5.6 m blank outer wall in a 40.5 m2 living room is a facade defect, not a furniture problem; the general rule is that a blank outer wall longer than 3 m in a habitable room must have a window or door added by the architect, and the furniture agent cannot fix it.

A nightstand in front of a window is acceptable when the window sill is at or above the nightstand's top (0.60 m); when the sill is at 0.20 m, the nightstand blocks the window and must be moved to the other side of the bed or the window sill raised; the general rule is that a nightstand in front of a window with a sill below 0.60 m is a conflict that must be resolved by moving the nightstand or raising the sill.

A coffee table overlapping an armchair by 0.12 m2 is a layout conflict; the general rule is that a coffee table must be at least 0.40 m from the front of every seat in the seating group, and when the drawn layout cannot satisfy this, the seating group must be re-solved as a unit, not the coffee table moved alone.

A sofa with no front (front_inferred) in a room with a clear open floor must have its front set to face the most open floor; the general rule is that a sofa drawn without a front in a room with a clear open floor must have its front set to face that floor, and the agent must use set_front, not move_piece or resize_piece.

A sofa's back must be on a wall; when the drawn position is 0.59 m off the nearest wall and no free wall span exists within 1.2 m of the drawn position, the sofa is a misread of a freestanding sofa or a sofa that belongs on a different wall, and the general rule is that a sofa drawn in the middle of a room with no wall behind it is a misread and must be moved to the nearest wall span or retyped.

A sofa drawn in a living room is a drawn anchor: the seating group is re-solved around it, and the agent may not move it to chase a walkway finding on a neighbour; a walkway that is blocked by the drawn sofa is a layout conflict to report, not a reason to relocate the anchor.

A drawn coffee table is locked to its drawn position (0.3 m, 1.2 m to a wall); when the drawn position does not sit in front of the sofa, the finding is a drawing/layout conflict to report, not a move the agent may make.

A washbasin that is part of a bath_set module is pinned to the module's counter: the agent may not swap its model to a freestanding one; a style finding on a module member is a style conflict to report, not a swap.

A toilet whose lowest point is 0.20 m above its floor is a parametric height error: the fix is to set its floor/height, not to swap its model; a swap that changes the height is refused by the fit rules.
A drawn bed is a drawn anchor: the agent may not move it to open a 0.60 m side walkway; a side gap that is too small is a layout conflict to report, not a move of the anchor.
A drawn coffee table that overlaps a drawn armchair by 0.12 m2 is a drawing conflict: the drawn_lock (0.3 m) forbids the move that would clear it, so the conflict is reported, not fixed by a move.

A drawn armchair that stands behind the back of the drawn sofa is a drawing conflict: rotating it to face the group is refused when it faces a wall or leaves the room, so the conflict is reported, not fixed by a rotation.

A drawn nightstand that stands in front of a window is a drawing conflict: the move that clears the window is refused (overlap with the bed, inside_room), so the conflict is reported, not fixed by a move.

A drawn wardrobe whose front clearance is 0.17 m (needs 0.80 m) is a drawing conflict: the move that opens the clearance is refused (no free wall span, still short), so the conflict is reported, not fixed by a move.

A washbasin that is part of a bath_set module and whose lowest point is 0.384 m above its floor is a module height error: the agent may not swap its model; the height must be corrected, which no tool in this run does.
